title: Entrusted (Kern ch. 27)
hookLine: the Buddha entrusts the teaching to the bodhisattvas; the Lotus closed

cards: A set of keys passes from one hand to another. A night nurse walks the morning shift through each patient's chart. A shop changes hands, and the old owner stands in the doorway one last time.
Handing something over is its own small ceremony, and the Lotus Sutra ends with one.
In the last chapter of Kern's ordering, the Buddha rises from his seat, turns to the great crowd of bodhisattvas, and gives them the teaching to carry.

teach.h: THE BUDDHA RISES FROM HIS SEAT.
teach.b: Here's the scene, paraphrased. The Buddha stands, and by his power he reaches out his right hand to the bodhisattvas. Over ages beyond counting, he says, I worked to reach this supreme awakening.
Now I hand it to you.

teach.h: TAKE IT, KEEP IT, MAKE IT KNOWN.
teach.b: Take it, keep it, and make it known widely, so that all beings may hear it.

teach.h: WE WILL DO AS THE LORD COMMANDS.
teach.b: The bodhisattvas bow, filled with joy, and answer together: we will do as the Lord commands. Do not be concerned. And they say it again.

Then the Buddha sends home the Buddhas who had gathered from other worlds to hear him, and the assembly rejoices. That's how the Lotus closes, in Kern's order: not with a final parable, but with a handoff.
The teaching doesn't stay with the teacher.

teach.h: THE WHOLE LOTUS, LOOKED BACK ON.
teach.b: Look back at the whole Lotus now. A ray of light from the Buddha's brow. Skillful means and one vehicle.
A burning house, a lost son, rain falling on every plant. A phantom city to rest in, and a jewel sewn in a coat. A stupa in the sky, and the dragon king's daughter.
Bodhisattvas rising from the cracks of the earth, and a Buddha whose life is long beyond counting.
Never Disparaging, bowing to everyone. Guanyin hearing cries. Two sons leading a king, and Samantabhadra's promise.
And at the end, a hand held out to the listeners: this is yours now.

how: Communities that keep the Lotus Sutra read its entrustment as the Buddha handing the teaching to the bodhisattvas, and some readers treat reciting, copying or teaching the sutra as a way of taking up that charge.

games.why: he reaches out his hand to the bodhisattvas and entrusts it to all of them: take it, keep it, make it known.

practice: Think of one thing you've been holding alone: a task, a family story only you remember, a way of making something. Bring to mind someone who could hold it, and picture handing it over, your hands empty afterward.
Notice whether you want to take it back; nothing needs deciding now.

wordCard.voice: Entrusted. The Lotus closes with the Buddha handing the teaching to the bodhisattvas: take it, keep it, make it known. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the title of the Lotus Sutra, the lotus of the true dharma. today it closes.
